gloss: make it happen; do it for someone
title: -kan
pattern: root + -kan: mati → matikan, kecil → kecilkan, beli → belikan (for someone) · Tolong …kan …
explanation: -kan makes something happen to something: mati (off, dead) → matikan (to switch off), bersih (clean) → bersihkan (to clean), kecil (small) → kecilkan (to make smaller, to turn down). With some verbs it means doing it for someone, who comes straight after: ambilkan saya air (get me some water), belikan saya pulsa (buy me some phone credit). The root + -kan on its own is the form for requests and instructions after tolong or silakan: Tolong matikan AC-nya, Silakan masukkan PIN Anda. In fuller sentences it comes with me- or di- as well (membersihkan, dibersihkan), and a dictionary lists it under the root.
natural: Polite requests about things around you: switching off, turning down, fetching, putting away. Tolong with the -kan form is polite enough for anyone, and Bisa tolong …? is softer still.
stiff: With friends, Jakarta-style speech swaps -kan for -in: matiin, ambilin, bersihin. Watch the spelling when the root ends in k: masuk + -kan is masukkan, with two k's.

gap.note: Matiin is the casual Jakarta-style form of the same word, fine with friends.
gap.why: Switching something off is making it mati: mati + -kan.

examples.english: Could you buy me some phone credit?

gap.why: Buying something for someone is beli + -kan, with the person straight after.

examples.english: Could you turn it down a bit?

gap.why: Making the sound smaller is kecil + -kan; mengecil is getting smaller by itself.
Putting the card in is masuk + -kan, with both k's; masuki is going into a place yourself.
